extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent examiners, IP policymakers, and practitioners assessing prior art
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of national standards and criteria used to determine whether a disclosure counts as prior art for novelty and inventive step (multiple jurisdictions: Norway, Paraguay, Poland, Portugal). Useful for examiners, litigators, and policymakers evaluating what types/qualities of disclosures defeat novelty or affect inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of prior art (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art is defined as: "Everything made available to the public, either in writing, orally, by exploitation or otherwise, shall be considered as known."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National pending applications published later affect novelty but not inventive step. The Norwegian Patent Office follows EPO Guidelines for public availability criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlimited means of disclosure (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: The means of disclosure that have an impact on novelty and inventive step are rather unlimited. No means of disclosure are excepted even if it may be difficult to substantiate the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Networks and communication such as www, chat groups, forums or e-mail may be either publicly available or limited; material on an unprotected web page is regarded as publication even if the page has not been visited. Evidence will be examined like other kinds of proof; archives are desirable to substantiate dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing/experimental-use exception (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary testing of an embodiment is an exception from the rule that novelty is damaged if the invention has been made available to an unlimited circle of people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant/inventor can substantiate that they made efforts to avoid public availability during testing, and the invention nonetheless became available despite such efforts, the invention is not regarded as publicly known.

rubrics_metrics.name: No age limit on prior art (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no age limit on prior art disclosures with regard to assessment of novelty and inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the fact that citations are old and that the need has existed for years may be used as an argument against an obviousness rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial irrelevance (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: A public disclosure anywhere is regarded as a public disclosure for the assessment of novelty and inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Norwegian law is applicable for the determination whether a disclosure has occurred; place of disclosure is irrelevant for the substantive assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person who disclosed is irrelevant (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Norwegian Patents Act makes no difference whether the information is disclosed by the applicant, inventor or by any other person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: a six months 'grace period' may be granted for disclosure by evident abuse (breaking confidentiality) or if the applicant displayed the invention at an official exhibition recognised by the Paris Convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for evident abuse / exhibitions (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: A six months 'grace period' may be granted if information about the invention is given by evident abuse or if the invention is disclosed through display by the applicant or predecessor at an official/recognised international exhibition (Paris Convention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enabling disclosure required (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be damaging for the novelty and inventive step a piece of information has to be an enabling disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the disclosure is not enabling due to errors and correction of the errors are not obvious to the skilled person, an erroneous disclosure will not be damaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability to an indefinite group suffices (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that the invention has been made publicly available is sufficient to damage novelty even if it is impossible to prove that anyone actually saw or accessed the information; availability to an indefinite group counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embodiment / reverse engineering as disclosure (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an embodiment is publicly accessible and it is possible to disassemble the embodiment to reveal the invention, this is regarded as a disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reverse engineering requires disassembly but special efforts were made to avoid such disassembly, public use of the embodiment is not regarded as a disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet treated like other media (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principally there is no difference if the information is on paper or as paperless information in an electronic network or through the internet; the question is whether it was made available to the public or only to a limited/confidential group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No special substantive rules for oral disclosure or other ways; evidence/substantiation of publication through new media is examined the same way as other proof; archives desirable to prove dates and changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for internet disclosure (Norway)
rubrics_metrics.description: The party invoking a piece of information must prove or substantiate that it was publicly available before the priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior art disclosure (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art disclosure destroys novelty and, given awareness, the invention would be obvious for any professional in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between novelty and inventive step (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any disclosure affects novelty; a simple disclosure of the invention does not necessarily affect the patent's inventive level (inventive step).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending applications considered in examination (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final examination includes the search for background information among pending applications filed prior to the examined patent; such pending applications may affect novelty and inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pending patent applications are included to the extent content is included in the prior application at time of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paraguay statutory definition of prior art (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state of prior art embraces everything disclosed or made available to the public, anywhere in the world, through tangible publication, oral disclosure, sales or trading, use or any other means, before the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State of prior art also includes content of pending patent applications at the Industrial Property Office with earlier filing/priority, but only to the extent included at publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local one‑year grace for inventor disclosures (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state of prior art will not embrace what has been published within the year prior to the filing date in Paraguay (or within the year prior to the filing date of which priority is invoked), as long as said disclosure resulted directly or indirectly from acts by the inventor or beneficiary, or from non‑fulfilment of a contract or illicit action against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclosure resulting from publication by an industrial property office is not covered by the exception unless the publication was by mistake or done by someone without right to obtain the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of disclosure unlimited (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognized means of disclosure: tangible publication, oral disclosure, sales or trading, use by any other means; law does not establish additional requirements for oral disclosure or disclosure by use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illicit/accidental disclosure exclusion (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information accidentally or intentionally placed through an illicit action is not comprehended in the state of the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and disclosures (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure carried out by a person bound by a confidentiality agreement is not considered part of the state of prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of errors in disclosed information (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors of the disclosed information are not comprehended in the state of prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse engineering / disassembly (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Possibility that a person might obtain information through additional steps (disassembly, reverse engineering) can constitute a disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, acts carried out without authorization of the inventor or owner constitute an infringement and illicit action, and therefore cannot be considered a disclosure that affects the state of prior art (Paraguayan view).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet can be prior art but needs special rules (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paperless information in an electronic network or through the internet could constitute sufficient disclosure to affect novelty or inventive step, but Internet requires special rules to determine when information constitutes a relevant and complete disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encryption, passwords, search engines and payment requirements matter; disclosures directed to a specific group (password-protected/scientific/professional) should not be considered as affecting novelty. Archives/files are necessary to prove disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence burden for internet disclosures (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: If information related to an invention is disclosed on the Internet, evidence must be presented by those interested in the patent not being granted (third parties may file observations/oppositions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There should be different levels of evidence for different kinds of disclosure; potential manipulation of internet information requires different standards; partial or incomplete internet disclosure does not destroy novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested internet disclosure criteria (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed criteria/rules to determine when internet disclosure is prior art: (a) easy access to said web sites; (b) clear and complete disclosure of an invention as a requirement; (c) easy understanding by a person familiar with the subject; (d) scientific, professional or educational goals pursued; (e) inventors' authorization or denial for said disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute novelty principle (Poland)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is new if it does not form part of the state of the art; state of the art is everything made available to the public by written or oral description, by use, displaying or disclosure in any other way before the priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete technical feature disclosure required to destroy novelty (Poland)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any disclosure destroys novelty; however, the invention is considered not novel when the complete set of its technical features is fully disclosed in the prior art. Separate disclosure of particular technical features does not by itself destroy novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If different features are disclosed in different publications and a skilled person could combine them to achieve the same result, that may render the invention obvious (lack of inventive step) rather than lack of novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending applications and their effect (Poland)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending applications of earlier priority not yet available to the public are considered prior art in assessment of novelty provided they will be published in the manner specified by law; those applications are not taken into consideration in assessment of inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wide range of evidence counts as disclosure (Poland)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means of disclosure include not only printed publications but also proofs of open use such as invoices, service manuals provided with goods to the market, certificates, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties may submit observations within six months from the date of publication of the patent application; such observations (evidence of prior art) are taken into account during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time/place/person irrelevant; secret/inaccessible information not prior art (Poland)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place of disclosure is irrelevant (even a unique publication in an exotic language or remote library counts); the fact of disclosure counts regardless of who disclosed or good/bad faith. Secret disclosure or information unavailable to the public (e.g., encrypted or protected) seems to be considered as not destroying novelty, unlike information available after payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on opponent (Poland)
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of proof should be on the party objecting the granting (or already granted) exclusive rights on the ground of lacking novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior art disclosure (Portugal)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art disclosure causes loss of novelty and inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portuguese Industrial Property Code (article 51) defines prior art and provides that pending applications (even unpublished) are included in the prior art; no differences between novelty and inventive step in effect under article 51.
